masthead.kicker: Hidden Champions of India / a DeepThought series

headline.text: Acme Corp: a demo wealth-creation engine, hidden in plain sight.

subhead.text: A fictional Pune widget maker that turns its own tooling R&D into products OEMs specify, used here to test the profile renderer end to end.

blocks.text: Revenue grew from ₹160 crore in FY23 to **₹250 crore in FY25**, about 25% a year. Profit grew faster: PAT from ₹18 crore to ₹38 crore.

It designs its own tooling: 22 of its 410 employees work in R&D, with 4 patents and an NABL-certified test lab. Widgets are 70% of revenue; fasteners and coatings the rest, sold to 300+ OEMs as AcmeGrip.
For scale, the fictional listed leader WidgetWorks earned an 18% EBITDA margin on ₹900 crore, growing about 6%. Acme is smaller, growing four times faster.

insights.point: The field is **large, and counted differently by different houses.**
insights.evidence: From ~$1.2B today toward $2B by 2030 (≈8%/yr) on the demo count. Acme, at ~₹250 Cr (~$30M), holds around 2.5% of it.

insights.point: OEMs buy on spec and price, but **repeat on delivery reliability.**
insights.evidence: Demo buyer research finds qualification cost keeps a supplier in once approved; switching is rare below a 5% price gap.

reflect.text: A patent-holding ~2.5% player in a market growing high single digits, with switching costs on its side. Demo text to verify the reflect block renders.

p3_opportunities.lede: Two demo openings, each built on something the fictional company already has.

items.title: Pricing the patents
items.body: AcmeGrip widgets outlast the commodity part by 2x in demo test data, yet are priced at channel parity. Worth asking: does the price reflect the extra life?

items.title: The OEMs already qualified
items.body: Acme is approved at 300 OEMs but actively ships to 180. The other 120 have already paid the qualification cost — reaching them is easier than winning new ones.

guesslabel.text: Possibilities, not prescriptions. Which would work, and how much, only Acme's own data and people can tell. Each is small, made to learn fast.

items.title: Test the price on two SKUs
items.body: Put the 2x-life test data in front of ten OEM buyers and see whether two flagship SKUs sell at a 10% premium.

items.title: Reactivate a sample of dormant OEMs
items.body: Pick 20 of the 120 qualified-but-inactive OEMs, give them one clear reason to order, and count how many come back and what it cost.

intro.text: A workflow is the set of steps a company runs to get a result. Below is how widget makers operate, matched to what the demo company states about its own.

steps: prototype & bench-test in the NABL lab

spotted.text: Spotted at "qualify": the durability proof stays in the lab, not carried to the price → pricing the patents.
Spotted at "reorder": 120 qualified OEMs never reorder → reactivate the dormant.
